summary: The root مَنَنَ primarily means to cut or break something. It also conveys the idea of weakness or failing strength.

headwords.def: مَنَّ عَلَيْهِ , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. مَنُنَ , (Msb,) inf. n. مَنٌّ (S, M, Msb, K) and مِنِّينَى ; (K;) and ; (Msb;) He conferred, or bestowed, upon him, a favour, or benefit. (S, M, Msb, K.) You say, مَنَّ عَلَيْهِ شَيْأً , and بِشَىْءٍ , which latter is more common, and عليه بِهِ He conferred, or bestowed, a thing upon him as a favour. (Msb.) مَنَّ عَلَيْهِ , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. مَنٌّ (T, Msb) or مِنَّةٌ ; (S, K;) and (S, M, Msb, K) and ; (M;) He reproached him for a favour, or benefit, which he (the former) had conferred, or bestowed; (M;) he recounted his gifts or actions to him. (Msb.) Ex., عَلَيْهَا بِمَا مَهَرَهَا [ He reproached her for the dowry he had given her ]. (K, art. مهر .) See Bd, ii. 264. See also an ex. in a verse cited voce

headwords.gloss: What?; O! what aileth mine eye, that its tears dry not?

parts.t: as in the following of El-Khansà,
أَلَا مَنْ لِعَيْنِى لَا تَجِفُّ دُمُوعُهَا
O! what aileth mine eye, that its tears dry not?

headwords.def: مَنْ [used for مَا in the sense of What? as in the following of El-Khansà, أَلَا مَنْ لِعَيْنِى لَا تَجِفُّ دُمُوعُهَا O! what aileth mine eye, that its tears dry not? quoted in the TA, art. فثأ .] مَنْ : respecting its dual مَنَانْ and مَنَيْنْ , and its pl. مَنُونْ and مَنِينْ , see I'Ak, p. 319. مَنْ لِى بِكَذَا : see بِ (near the end of the paragraph).

headwords.gloss: Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies; Zeyd is more reasonable than that he will lie; Zeyd is too reasonable to lie

parts.t: Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies:
but, though this is the virtual meaning, the proper explanation, accord. to modern usage, is, that
; for in a phrase of this kind, an adjunct pronoun is sometimes expressed; so that the aor. must be marfooa; and the literal meaning is,
Zeyd is more reasonable than that he will lie;
Zeyd is too reasonable to lie.
It may be doubted, however, whether a phrase of this kind be of classical authority. The only other instance that I have found is
هُوَ أَحْصَنُ مِنْ أَنْ يْرَام وَأَعَزُّ

headwords.def: مِنْ : زَيْدٌ أَعْقَلُ مِنْ أَنْ يَكْذِب means مِنَ الذَِّى يَكْذِبُ (Kull, p. 78) [i. e. Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies: but, though this is the virtual meaning, the proper explanation, accord. to modern usage, is, that أَنْ is here for أَنَّ with the adjunct pronoun هُ ; for in a phrase of this kind, an adjunct pronoun is sometimes expressed; so that the aor. must be marfooa; and the literal meaning is, Zeyd is more reasonable than that he will lie; which is equivalent to saying, Zeyd is too reasonable to lie. It may be doubted, however, whether a phrase of this kind be of classical authority. The only other instance that I have found is هُوَ أَحْصَنُ مِنْ أَنْ يْرَام وَأَعَزُّ مِن أَنْ يُضَام , in the TA, voce
مُنَ ٱللّٰهِ is for أَيْمُنُ اللّٰه .

headwords.gloss: An obligation; upon one; to him

parts.t: (M, Msb.) Also an inf. n. See

headwords.def: مِنَّةٌ [ An obligation, عَلَى أَحَدٍ upon one, and also لَهُ to him. ] A favour, or benefit, conferred, or bestowed. (M, Msb.) Also an inf. n. See مَنَّ عَلَيْهِ .

headwords.gloss: I will not do it till the end of time

parts.t: I will not do it till the end of time.
is fem. and sing. and pl. (Fr, S.)

headwords.def: لَا أَفْعَلُهُ أُخْرَى المَنُونِ I will not do it till the end of time. (S.) مَنُونٌ is fem. and sing. and pl. (Fr, S.)

headwords.gloss: The first; or main; rope of a well
headwords.def: مَنِينٌ The first ( or main ) rope of a well. See كَرَبٌ .

headwords.gloss: Very bountiful; beneficent; Very reproachful for his gifts

parts.t: one who gives nothing without reproaching for it and making account of it:

headwords.def: مَنَّانٌ Very bountiful or beneficent. Also [ Very reproachful for his gifts; ] one who gives nothing without reproaching for it and making account of it: an intensive epithet. (TA.)
اِمْتِنَانِىٌّ Gratuitous; granted as a favour: opposed to وُجُوبِىٌّ .

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
